facts.text: Cherry Hill Farmhouse opens its historic doors for free public tours every Saturday from April to October, 10 a.m. to noon.
Visitors can grind corn in the Barn’s period machines, a hands‑on activity that brings 19th‑century farming to life.
The Friends of Cherry Hill host seasonal teas, including Valentine’s and Mother’s Day, where guests enjoy early‑afternoon refreshments in the historic farmhouse.
Private tours of Cherry Hill Farmhouse are available year‑round, costing $5 per person and offering a deeper dive into mid‑19th‑century rural Virginia life.
Two Girl Scout programs at Cherry Hill let scouts play Victorian‑era parlor games, write with quill pens, and earn badges in a historic setting.
From June to August, the City of Falls Church runs week‑long summer history camps at Cherry Hill, letting children experience 19th‑century Virginia firsthand.
